t: its `id`, `name`, `kind`, `isDefault`,\n`needsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No\nroute ret

urns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an account

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is al
ways\nread as an id: it matches that account or answers `404`, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is
a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no account has makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A n

ame two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, start
s with a letter or digit, and\nis at most 64 characters. One outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is

refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are
unique on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing
checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own label, and\n replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep

each name
 for one test user.
* **Uploaded accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local
 app, browser or s
andbox ever receives their token, the account's owner\n included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **T
he token is bound to the server URL saved in the project.** The body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (
`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the r
oute doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is at most 16 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When C
I uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when the issuer rejects our refreshes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-l
ived credential. Without one, an\n expired account lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restore
s it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and server: 60, refilling at 120 an\n hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-

After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as the person who created it, with all of that person's
access. For personal acc
ounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who\nis not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\ns
erver shared with the project, accounts are project accounts: only a project\nadmin can upload, rename or delete them, and every m

ember's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running evals as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's *

*default** account.
To run evals from CI as one account, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash t
heme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PATCH \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_
ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\

n -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which
reads the tok
en from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://do
cs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-commands).\n\nThe default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't ru
n the same\nkey's runs at the same time with different defaults. Where your organization\nhas account choice for eval suites, a su
ite can instead save the accounts it\nruns as, in its settings in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those\naccounts and igno

res the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer
to
revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,\nand it also ends any copy of the same token you still

hold. The default
account can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.

### T

he deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the
accounts API shipped.
It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ impo

rted, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An accoun
t this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes\ninto keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the U
RL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted

and ignored. Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `de
tails.code` are listed in the\n[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors

).

## Run evals from the API

The shortest useful loop — create a run with one inline test, then poll:

```bash theme={"th
eme\":\"css-variables\"}\n# 1. Create (responds 202 immediately; -f + jq -e fail fast on errors)\nRUN_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST \\\n
\"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Co

ntent-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{
 "suiteName": "smoke",
 "serverIds": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],
 "tests":

[{
 "title": "echo works",
 "runs": 1,
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
 "provider": "

anthropic",
 "steps": [
 { "id": "s1", "kind": "prompt", "prompt": "Use the echo tool to say hi" },
/app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 3. If it d
id not pass, read the decision summary FIRST\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decis
ion-summary\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration tool calls, token usage,
latency\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bea

rer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every
client reads a run t
he same way. Four things to know before gating on it:\n\n* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading th
e\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they ar
e trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each — 3 against 15 for three cases run five times —\n so a count wit
hout its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted\n across that line.\n* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides
it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit undernea
